Radiology Report
Date: 08/12/2026
Patient: Sharan Wisozk, 87 y/o F

MRI lumbar spine 08/12/2026: L5-S1 disc herniation with moderate left foraminal stenosis contacting the exiting nerve root.

Findings: The lumbar spine demonstrates normal alignment. No evidence of vertebral body compression fractures. The L5-S1 level shows a disc herniation causing moderate left foraminal stenosis. This stenosis contacts the exiting left S1 nerve root. No significant central canal stenosis noted. Adjacent discs show mild degenerative changes without significant protrusion or extrusion.

Impression: L5-S1 disc herniation with moderate left foraminal stenosis contacting the exiting nerve root. No other acute abnormalities identified.

Pain Management Consultation
Date: 09/12/2026
Patient: Sharan Wisozk, 87 y/o F

HPI: LBP x10 wks w/ radiation to L LE. Pt reports worsening pain, no relief with OTC meds.

Exam: Tenderness noted over lumbar paraspinals. Limited ROM due to pain. Neuro exam: LLE weakness 4/5, diminished sensation in L4-L5 dermatomes.

Labs: Notable: fever to 38.6 C and ESR 88 concerning for discitis.

Plan: Admit for IV abx, MRI lumbar spine to evaluate for infectious etiology. Pain control with cautious opioid use. Monitor neuro status closely.

Follow-up: Reassess after imaging and labs. Consult ID and ortho as needed.
